newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina Senate sues governor over vetoes.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina Senate sues governor over vetoes.

text.p: The South Carolina Senate sued Gov. David Beasley, charging that he unconstitutionally vetoed individual words and sentences in the state budget.

In a lawsuit filed Wednesday, the Democratic-majority Senate asked the state Supreme Court to overturn the Republican governor's vetoes, which were sustained by the House of Representatives last month.

Beasley has a line-item veto. But the Senate argued that by vetoeing individual words, phrases and paragraphs within budget items, he had in effect written law and exceeded his constitutional authority.
Beasley spokesman Gary Karr called the lawsuit pointless and a waste of taxpayer money.
"The governor believes he has the power to do what he did," Karr told The State newspaper.

Beasley's vetoes included eliminating a clause that would have eased restrictions on how much money video poker players can win in a 24-hour period. The change would have allowed players to win back the amount they lost during a 24-hour span in addition to the $125 cap on winnings.

Beasley also cut two sentences requiring the state Ethics Commisson to investigate maintenance logs of state-owned aircraft. Several fees for records searches at the state Department of Health and Environmental Control were also axed.

Karr said many issues raised in the lawsuit had been dealt with in a 1995 lawsuit involving the governor's veto powers. In that case, the state Supreme Court ruled Beasley acted within his authority when he vetoed entire subsections of the budget dealing with video poker regulation.
The 1995 ruling did not address the elimination of individual words and sentences.
